results.fact: Approach describes a different peak (Inspiration Peak via Terror Basin)
results.correct_value: Goodell Creek roadbed, Terror Creek climbers' path, across the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin below the Blob
results.evidence: The first-ascent report places the route on the Blob in the remote Crescent Creek Basin of the Southern Pickets. A Pickets reference site lists The Rake (The Blob) among the Southern Pickets and describes reaching Crescent Creek Basin from the Goodell Creek roadbed, including the Barrier crossing (low and high options, recommended from Terror Basin). An independent trip report reached Crescent Creek Basin from Goodell Creek via Terror Creek camp and a path up the Barrier, and calls the peak 'The Rake (aka The Blob)'. The approach text was copied from an Inspiration Peak row.

patches.fact: Approach describes a different peak (Inspiration Peak via Terror Basin)
patches.find: Inspiration Peak shares the same approach as West McMillan Spire: from Goodell Creek Campground, an unmaintained path climbs the Goodell Creek valley for roughly 4 to 4.5 miles before a steep, brushy climbers' track gains about 1,500 feet in under half a mile to reach the alpine notch above Terror Basin, the standard base camp for the Southern Pickets. From camp, reaching Inspiration Peak involves traversing heather and snow slopes and crossing a permanent snowfield near the col between it and West McMillan Spire before tackling a technical rock route (low 5th class up to 5.9 depending on the line).
patches.replace: From the Goodell Creek group-camp trailhead near Newhalem, walk the overgrown Goodell Creek roadbed for about 4 miles to the cairn near the Terror Creek crossing, then climb the Terror Creek climbers' path. The Blob stands above Crescent Creek Basin, so from the Terror Creek side you must cross the Barrier, the loose, brushy ridge dividing the Terror Creek drainage from Crescent Creek; it can be crossed low or high from Terror Basin. Descend into Crescent Creek Basin and camp within reach of the Himmelhorn and the Blob, then scramble to the base of the south buttress.

results.correct_value: 7840 ft (summit of The Rake / The Blob)
results.evidence: The first-ascent report says the route tops out on the summit of the Blob. The Pickets reference site lists The Rake (The Blob) at 7,840 ft and the Picket Range encyclopedia entry lists The Rake at 7,840 ft (2,390 m). high_point_ft is right; the Summit pin's 7,337 is the outlier. (The area record and the Junction pin at the same coordinate also carry 7,337 - see the discovered entry.)

results.correct_value: No park entrance fee; overnight backcountry permit $10/person + $6 permit fee (summer season); land manager NPS
results.evidence: The park's fees page says there is no fee to enter the North Cascades NPS Complex and that backcountry permits cost $10 per person plus a $6 non-refundable fee; the park's fee-change news release gives the same figures for the mid-May to early-October season. The Southern Pickets lie inside North Cascades National Park, so the Forest Service land manager and 'free self-issue permit' in _raw are wrong. fees is written as a scoped negative per the settled convention.

results.correct_value: Access Col (~6,100 ft) and Luna Col (~7,200 ft) are two places; Access Col is gained first
results.evidence: One trip report climbs a scree chute from Access Creek Basin (4,300 ft) to the 6,100-ft Access Col southwest of the basin, then traverses onward toward Luna. The Luna Peak route description puts Luna Col at 7,200 ft, the notch beside Luna Peak reached across a basin at about 6,600 ft. They are separate cols, so the approach's 'Luna Col/Access Creek Col' is wrong; the bivy card's sequence is right.
